fumigation of fruit with acetic acid vapors at low concentrations (2.0 to 5.4 milligrams per liter) prevented postharvest decay by several important postharvest fungal pathogens.

fumigation with acetic acid (AA), as a vapor at concentrations as low as 2.0 to 2.7 milligrams per liter, was effective in preventing decay by postharvet fungi of apples, pears, tomatoes, oranges, and kiwifrut, and grapes.

acetic acid fumigation at concentrations as low as 2 mg/liter in air can prevent postharvest decay in fruit and vegetables caused by a variety of postharvest fungi and that fumigation at temperatures as low as 1C can prevent fruit decay.

fumigation with low levels of acetic acid vapors is an effective method for the control of postharvest decay in fruit and vegetables.
